- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast drop, it often overcorrects; cap peak forecast at 2–3% above recent high.
- If sentiment includes multiple negative spikes (e.g., -0.61, -0.22), model frequently underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- Model often lags in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 3 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is flat or mildly positive (0.06–0.17) and model is overconfident, apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overestimating mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–15 days, model often fails to recognize it — apply a 2–5% downward bias starting from day 10.
